Analysis document: [https://github.com/wildfly/wildfly-proposals/pull/797|https://github.com/wildfly/wildfly-proposals/pull/797|smart-link] 



This work item involved planning the addition of gRPC support to WildFly, which is currently in the planning stage.

* The team discussed removing the dependency on the feature pack, as it was no longer considered a blocker.
* It was confirmed that the work is not blocked by the feature pack, and the dependency was removed.
* The scope was refined to focus on core features, with considerations for splitting the implementation into smaller, manageable RFEs due to its size.
* Limitations related to gRPC deployment, such as supporting only one deployment per server and versioning concerns, were identified as key technical considerations.
* The team agreed to support CDI injection only, excluding REST, EJB, security, CLI, web-console, and graceful shutdown initially, with potential follow-up RFEs for these features.
* The target release for gRPC support was set for WildFly 8.2, aligning with its roadmap, and further analysis and sizing are ongoing.

Bootable jar runtime mechanism for base EAP was introduced in EAP 8.1 on Baremental. Now, this Jira is used to track achieving the same on OpenShift platforms. 

Measure and document the performance improvement. 

Provides support for running microservice apps without the need archive it as a deployment and without the need to deploy it in a running application server.
Provides support for ability to run microservice apps on the Operating Systems command line as a bootable jar.
Provides support for developing and running the app. "java -jar app.jar" and maven command line interface.

Provides support for running these microservices apps in OpenShift. (Per discussions with Engineering, this capability, i.e. running on OpenShift isn't provided with 8.1 version yet, it would be targeted in a future version)
